summary: Reproduced event-loop starvation in synchronous OpenAI request conversion, the regular TokenizerManager fallback, and the real ASGI /v1/chat/completions versus /ping route. Blocking preprocessing now runs in a TokenizerManager-owned single-thread executor with context propagation; mock or alternate managers fall back to asyncio.to_thread.

tests.what_was_measured: A concurrent coroutine was starved for one second by synchronous OpenAI request conversion.
A concurrent coroutine was starved for one second by the regular tokenizer fallback.
The real ASGI /ping route was starved while /v1/chat/completions performed synchronous conversion.
207 tests and 72 subtests passed, including responsiveness, executor serialization, context propagation, and related OpenAI request behavior.
The real ASGI /ping route remained responsive during blocked chat preprocessing.
All changed Python source and regression files compiled successfully.
Registered-test placement and metadata validation passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: The reproduced defect is CPU-side asyncio event-loop starvation before scheduler or GPU execution; no model weights or GPU inference were needed or claimed.

remaining_limitations: No full model serving or GPU inference run was performed; this validates HTTP transport scheduling and preprocessing behavior, not model architecture behavior, semantic accuracy, or distributed execution.
The upstream companion PR remains open, so this mirror change may need reconciliation if upstream adopts a different executor lifecycle or concurrency policy.
ruff was not installed in the prepared interpreter; py_compile, registered-test validation, focused regressions, ASGI integration, and related unit suites were run instead.
